messages:
maya: Proposal: start a new synthetic generator called 'weave' for apples-to-apples perf comparisons. Goals: deterministic seeding, configurable microburst lattice, KV cold->warm transitions, and long-tail latency shaping. I sketched a minimal config below. Thoughts?

oliver: love the name. key thing: make the seed deterministic across kernel variations so we can compare kernel-selection changes without traffic noise. also need a mode that replays real traces but maps them to our batcher semantics.

devon: agree. also: we should model KV cache behavior explicitly. currently our replay harness pretends KV is instant warm; that masks cold-start overheads when kernel switches change KV access patterns.

maya: exactly. thinking of two KV modes: 'steady' (kv warmed for prefix of requests) and 'episodic' (periodic cold windows where we evict). The generator should annotate requests with a "kv_state" tag so the runtime can optionally simulate lookup latency.

samir: can we make the kv_state transitions driven by a small state machine? e.g. after N unique prefixes -> warm, after idle T -> evict. That would emulate real client patterns (bursty chat vs single-shot requests).

maya: yeah. draft config snippet: ```json
{
  "seed": 12345,
  "qps_profile": {"type":"sawtooth","min":5,"max":200,"period_s":60},
  "burst_lattice": {"lanes":4,"spike_width_ms":50,"jitter_ms":10},
  "kv_policy": {"mode":"episodic","warm_after_unique":8,"evict_after_s":30},
  "replay_mapping": {"enable":true,"map_sessions_to_shards":true}
}
```

oliver: couple of suggestions: 1) add a 'prefix_length_dist' so we can control average sequence lengths (affects KV hit rate and batch shape). 2) make qps_profile support 'flat-with-probes' to insert isolated high-latency probes for tail shaping.

devon: for apples-to-apples when testing kernel selection, we must capture and replay the exact inter-arrival jitter. The batcher respects absolute arrival times; if the generator smooths jitter, it's not comparable. So include an 'emit_raw_timestamps' flag.

maya: good call. also add a 'kernel_probe' mode that forces the runtime to choose each kernel variant for a short window (rotate through kernels) so we get side-by-side metrics in one run. perf-bot can annotate transitions.

perf-bot: autopost: ran 2-min baseline (seed=12345) vs kernel rotate. Summary: avg latency 42ms -> kernelB avg 40ms, p95 improved 12% during kernelC, but KV-cold tail increased when kernelB used float32 path. Full logs: https://internal/redwood/bench/2212345678

samir: that is interesting — kernelB reduces avg but hurts KV-cold tail. suggests kernelB's memcpy pattern interferes with KV async completion. we should add a 'kv_io_latency' knob to the generator to stress that path.

maya: action items: (1) oliver add prefix_length_dist and emit_raw_timestamps flags to generator by EOD, (2) devon add kv_state annotations and episodic policy, (3) samir add kv_io_latency knob and a small script to correlate kernel windows with tail spikes, (4) perf-bot run a kernel-rotation job once generator updated.

oliver: I'll PR config schema and a tiny CLI to produce ndjson events with exact timestamps. will add tests to ensure deterministic ordering with seed.

devon: I'll prototype kv_state FSM and add unit test that simulates 10000 sessions and asserts expected warm/cold ratios for given params.

samir: I'll instrument runtime to log "kernel-window-start" and "kv-io-latency" metrics with the run id tag so we can join events later.

maya: perfect. one more note: let's keep threads short in the harness output; we don't want extremely long single-session chains because that blows up KV memory sim. maybe cap session length and model repeat sessions.

oliver: ack. thinking default session cap 64 tokens. config will allow longer for heavy tests.

maya: cool. I'll file a follow-up doc in the perf repo with the config proposal and example outputs. thanks all :) :rocket:
